# Introduction

## Problem Statement

Salesforce adoption may vary across field users. Some users may enter information consistently, while others may use the system only when required.

Inconsistent adoption can create problems with:

- Data completeness
- Documentation timeliness
- Workflow consistency
- Visibility into field activity

::: {.notes}
The problem is not simply whether employees have access to Salesforce. The larger issue is whether they use it consistently and meaningfully in their daily work.
:::

## Analytics Objective

> Evaluate whether a targeted field engagement intervention improves meaningful Salesforce adoption, data quality, and user perceptions.

The evaluation will compare outcomes before and after the intervention. A comparison group will be used when operationally feasible.

## Why This Matters

Better Salesforce adoption can help the organization:

- Make field activity more visible
- Improve the quality of CRM records
- Identify workflow barriers
- Support more consistent decision-making

The results can show whether the intervention is useful and which parts should be improved.

# Literature and Project Rationale

## Meaningful Technology Adoption

Technology adoption is more than simply having access to a system. Meaningful adoption includes repeated use, complete records, timely documentation, and behavior that supports the intended workflow.

For this project, Salesforce adoption will be treated as a multidimensional outcome rather than one single login measure.

## Evaluation Logic

The project follows a simple evaluation logic:

1. Establish a baseline.
2. Deliver a targeted engagement intervention.
3. Measure adoption and perceptions again.
4. Compare the change over time.

This design connects the intervention to measurable behavioral and attitudinal outcomes.

## Research Gap and Project Contribution

A basic usage count may not explain whether Salesforce is being used effectively. This project adds value by combining:

- Behavioral CRM indicators
- Data-quality indicators
- User perceptions and barriers
- Before-and-after comparison

# Methods

## Data and Sampling

The project will use field users who work with Salesforce.

Potential data sources include:

- Salesforce activity records
- Record-completeness checks
- Documentation timestamps
- A short user survey or interview

Users may be divided into a pilot group receiving the intervention and a comparison group when feasible.

## Intervention Plan

The intervention may include:

- A short Salesforce training session
- A workflow demonstration
- Examples of complete and useful records
- A quick-reference guide
- Follow-up reminders or check-ins

The intervention should address barriers identified during the baseline assessment.

## Measures

| Outcome | Example measure | Expected direction |
|---|---|---|
| Platform engagement | Relevant Salesforce activity or usage frequency | Increase |
| Data completeness | Percentage of required fields completed | Increase |
| Documentation timeliness | Time between activity and documentation | Improve |
| Workflow consistency | Percentage of records following the expected process | Increase |
| User perception | Confidence and perceived usefulness survey scores | Increase |

## Analysis Plan

The analysis will compare:

- Baseline versus post-intervention results
- Pilot group versus comparison group, when available
- Changes across different user segments
- Behavioral outcomes and user perceptions

Possible statistics include means, percentages, change scores, and simple pre/post comparisons.

# Illustrative Analysis

## Reproducible Example

The following example uses illustrative planning data. It is not presented as actual company results.

```{r}
#| label: fig-adoption-change
#| fig-cap: "Illustrative change in meaningful Salesforce adoption"
#| fig-width: 8
#| fig-height: 4.5

period <- c("Baseline", "Post-intervention")
adoption <- c(52, 68)

barplot(
  adoption,
  names.arg = period,
  col = c("#9ecae1", "#2171b5"),
  ylim = c(0, 100),
  ylab = "Meaningful adoption (%)",
  main = "Illustrative Pre/Post Comparison"
)
text(
  x = c(0.7, 1.9),
  y = adoption + 5,
  labels = paste0(adoption, "%")
)
```

## Interpreting the Example

In this illustrative example, meaningful adoption increases from 52% to 68% after the intervention.

The actual project should only interpret the intervention as effective after checking:

- Whether the change is consistent across users
- Whether the comparison group changed differently
- Whether data quality also improved
- Whether user perceptions support the behavioral findings

## Limitations

- The intervention may not be randomly assigned.
- Users may differ in role, experience, or workload.
- A short follow-up period may not show long-term adoption.
- CRM records may not capture every type of user behavior.
- Survey responses may be affected by social desirability.

# Conclusion

## Key Takeaways

- Salesforce adoption should be measured using multiple indicators.
- The intervention should respond to documented user barriers.
- A baseline and post-intervention comparison can show whether outcomes changed.
- A comparison group strengthens the evaluation when it is operationally possible.
- Behavioral and perception data should be interpreted together.

## Expected Contribution

This project can help the CEP team determine whether targeted field engagement improves Salesforce use in a meaningful way.

The results can also guide future training, workflow design, and internal communication.
